input: Research cold-pressed juicing equipment for home use

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Cold-press juicers vary widely — knowing whether the user wants to compare multiple machines, find one specific recommendation, or understand the technology broadly changes how deep and wide the research needs to go.
Whether this is for a single person, a couple, or a family affects the required capacity, motor power, and yield expectations of the machine being researched.

How often and what types of produce (leafy greens, hard vegetables, citrus, wheatgrass) the user plans to juice determines which machine features actually matter — some juicers excel at greens, others at hard produce.
Cold-press juicers range from $80 to over $700. A budget ceiling immediately filters out a large portion of the market and shapes which models are worth researching.
Counter space and storage constraints at home directly affect whether a vertical, horizontal, or twin-gear juicer is even viable — some models are large and heavy.

Some users prioritise ease of cleaning above all, others want maximum juice yield, quiet operation, or a specific aesthetic — knowing the priority order prevents recommending a technically superior but practically wrong machine.
Understanding what the output of this research looks like — a shortlist of 3 models, a comparison table, a single buy recommendation — determines the format and depth of the final deliverable.

gold.taskTitle: Research cold-pressed juicing equipment for home
gold.taskDescription: Find and evaluate cold-press (slow/masticating) juicers suitable for home use, covering options, features, and a purchase decision.

questions.title: What is the main goal of this research — compare models, pick one, or learn the technology?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants a broad overview of cold-press juicer types, a curated shortlist, or a single definitive recommendation to act on.

questions.title: How many people will this juicer regularly serve?
questions.description: Determine household size to gauge the required capacity, feed chute size, and how much juice volume per session is needed.

questions.title: What produce do you plan to juice most — greens, hard vegetables, citrus, or a mix?
questions.description: Identify the primary produce types to focus research on machines optimised for those inputs, since performance varies significantly by produce category.

questions.title: What is your maximum budget for this equipment?
questions.description: Establish a spending ceiling to filter the market and avoid wasting research time on models outside the user's financial range.

questions.title: How much counter or storage space can you dedicate to this machine?
questions.description: Determine physical space available so the research can exclude juicer form factors that simply will not fit the user's kitchen setup.

questions.title: What matters most to you — easy cleaning, juice yield, quiet motor, or something else?
questions.description: Identify the user's top priority feature so that trade-off decisions in the research are made with the right emphasis.

questions.title: What should the final research output look like — a comparison table, a shortlist, or a single pick?
questions.description: Define what a completed, useful deliverable looks like so the research is structured to end in the right format for the user.
